_meta.description: Composed into vhir-json and vhir-delimited. Objects, arrays of objects and dotted keys use OpenSearch's default object mapping, so nested fields keep their names and stay searchable and aggregatable. Numbers and dates get field-level ignore_malformed with the types dynamic mapping would choose, so a value of the wrong type is dropped from that field (marked in _ignored) and the record is kept. A field that is a scalar in one record and an object in another is rejected per record with the reason. There are no object templates: the earlier ones used `flattened`, which is not an OpenSearch type, and rejected every record containing an object or a dotted key. source.ip is mapped ip, as the evtx indices map it, with ignore_malformed: a CSV value that is not an address (`*`, `[::]`) is dropped from the field and the row kept, and one aggregation across json, delimited and evtx indices reads addresses instead of the raw bytes a keyword/ip mix returns. It is a dynamic template, first, for strings only: declaring source.ip as a property made `source` an object, which rejected every record with a scalar `source` column (syslog, firewall and generic CSV exports), and a rule without the string match mapped an object at source.ip as ip, dropping its contents unmarked.
